messages:
Michael (Support): Hey team, customer @layla_customer reporting a spike of 429s hitting /v1/rerank since ~08:10 UTC. They say it started after a client release. Error payload: "status: 429, code: quota_exceeded". Can someone triage?
Layla (Customer): Here's a sample request from our logs — we started seeing this at 08:09:34: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"query": "best hotels in SF", "candidates": ["... repeated ~200 items ..."]}'
```
We have ~10 clients (same API key) doing parallel calls, each sending ~200 candidates. Response headers show:
```
x-ratelimit-limit-rerank: 100
x-ratelimit-remaining-rerank: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 1719904040
retry-after: 15
```
Layla (Customer): Also seeing very high tail latency when successful responses do come back (p95 ~ 1.6s). Any quick mitigations?
Julien (SRE): I pulled internal limiter logs for acct: acct_r42 — we hit the per-account QPS cap repeatedly starting 08:09:30. Log excerpt: `throttle: account=acct_r42 route=/v1/rerank qps=120.4 limit=100 window=1s` — so that's a hard QPS throttle, not token burn.
Sara (Engineer): Thanks @julien. Two immediate items: 1) confirm if limiter counts requests only or weighted by candidate_count; in our current config rerank is request-count-only, so large candidate lists don't change QPS limit but do increase work per-request and can increase latency/backpressure. 2) Need a repro with a client that mimics ~10 parallel clients @200 candidates to reproduce in staging.
Michael (Support): Customer asks whether they can get a temporary bump to reduce user impact. What's safe?
Julien (SRE): I can temporarily raise acct_r42 limit to 150 QPS for the next 48h while they roll out a fix. Will monitor error rates + p99 latency. Doing now.
ops-bot: quota-change: account=acct_r42 action=temporary_bump new_limit=150 duration=48h actor=julien_sre ticket=RERANK-312
Layla (Customer): Thanks — that helps. We'll also patch client to cap candidates to 50 and implement client-side exponential backoff on 429s.
Sara (Engineer): For long-term: recommend they either 1) reduce candidate_count, or 2) batch candidates into fewer logical rerank calls with pre-filtering upstream, or 3) contact sales for Dedicated capacity if steady QPS > 100. Added integration note to RERANK-312: include example backoff code and headers to check (`Retry-After`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-rerank`).
Michael (Support): Created support ticket SUP-9071 linking to RERANK-312 and included sample logs. Customer asked for guidance on interpreting headers — I linked docs: https://docs.redwood.com/rerank#rate-limits
Julien (SRE): Monitoring note: after bump, 429 rate dropped to near-zero in 5m, p95 latency still high for a bit but trending down. We'll close the emergency loop after 24h stability.
Layla (Customer): Confirmed green for now, will redeploy the client change in the morning. Appreciate the fast turnaround :white_check_mark:.
Michael (Support): Follow-up actions: 1) engineering to publish a short guidance blob on recommended max_candidate_count (sara to own). 2) SRE to revert temporary bump after 48h unless customer requests extension. 3) Support to confirm customer patch on next business day and close SUP-9071.
Sara (Engineer): On it — drafting doc with sample client backoff and a recommended default max_candidates=50 + example curl and pseudo-code. Will reference in RERANK-312.
Julien (SRE): Setting an alert to watch account acct_r42 qps >120 for 6h window.
Michael (Support): Thanks everyone — keeping thread open until customer confirms patch deployed.
